title: Etale-proetale comparison for supported sections and their exterior products
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $A$ a finite commutative ring. All coefficient categories below are ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf of rings $A$, not condensed coefficient categories. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], separated in the diagonal sense [def-weil-proper-morphism], a closed subscheme $C\subseteq T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $M\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with its bounded-below inverse image as in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
c^C_{T,M}:R\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{et}},M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\nu_T^*M),
$$
natural in $M$ and compatible with open restriction and forgetting supports. Here both support functors are the ordinary right-derived sections with support [def-pur-support-cohomology]. For $C=T$ this map is the global-sections comparison induced by the comparison adjunction unit.

Let $Z\subseteq X$ and $W\subseteq Y$ be closed subschemes of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and suppose $F=K\boxtimes_A^L L$ is bounded below. Products are fibre products over $k$ [def-pc-base-change], with projections $p_X,p_Y$, and $K\boxtimes_A^L L$ means $p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$. Put $K_p=\nu_X^*K$, $L_p=\nu_Y^*L$, $P=X\times_kY$. Let
$$
\theta:\nu_P^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}K_p\boxtimes_A^L L_p
$$
be the composite of the canonical derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the comparison pullback identifications [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The supported exterior products [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] in the two topologies satisfy the equality in $D(A)$, the unbounded derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$
R\Gamma_{Z\times_kW}(P_{\mathrm{proet}},\theta)\circ c^{Z\times_kW}_{P,F}\circ\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}
=\kappa^{Z,W}_{K_p,L_p}\circ(c^Z_{X,K}\otimes_A^Lc^W_{Y,L}).
$$
The pro-etale exterior product here is defined by pulling back and tensoring supported sections, derived with K-flat tensor and injective support resolutions in that topology. The assertion concerns comparison of these maps; it does not assert a Kunneth isomorphism in either topology.

proof.text: Identify the global-section support kernel with terminal evaluation by preservation of kernels, normalized after the kernel inclusion. Derive this natural isomorphism and identify the given comparison with derived base change of the normalized ordinary unit. Naturality of derived base change proves the forgetting square. At full support, evaluation on the empty complement is zero, so the support inclusions are isomorphisms. Apply the existing finite-coefficient comparison-unit theorem to prove invertibility.

proof.text: Compose the normalized etale supported-coefficient adjunction with comparison pullback and transport its right adjoint by the kernel-evaluation isomorphism. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives the coefficient comparison. Its inverse is the left mate of the actual support comparison. Checking after the monic support inclusion identifies the comparison on quotient generators with the constant-sheaf comparison. The derived-mate theorem identifies its exact derived map with the mate of derived support comparison.

proof.text: Construct the constant-sheaf comparison by uniqueness of left adjoints. Its terminal-evaluation presentation is monoidal, because the adjunctions and the direct-image terminal evaluation are monoidal. Identify the canonical constant pullback isomorphisms with the inverse-image adjunct of the constant direct-image map. The composite-adjunction Hom bijections then give the comparison/pullback square with the specified coefficient transport.

proof.text: Precompose the ordinary supported tensor square with the epimorphic product-support quotient map. Both paths become constant tensor multiplication followed by the two pulled-back quotient maps. The constant comparison is monoidal, and its pullback square identifies those two projection quotient maps. Cancel the product quotient to prove the coefficient tensor square.

proof.text: Lift the ordinary coefficient tensor square to signed total complexes and then to derived categories using the model-normalized derived tensor API. Normalize the exact derived maps by their complex factorization isomorphisms; conjugating the left-derived tensor comparison to the exact derived functor gives exactly the specified tensor component of theta. The etale and pro-etale coefficient comparisons satisfy their unique complex-model normalizations, so localization gives the required derived coefficient tensor square. Carry out the conversion between the two signed-complex comparison APIs and the ordinary-to-complex square inside the generic coefficient argument, before specializing. Construct the pro-etale natural transformation and its component normalization first for an arbitrary coefficient category, then specialize to ModuleCat A; this retains the existing derived tensor presentation without unfolding sheaf tensor data.

proof.text: Transport each pulled-back evaluation counit by the derived comparison mate and the canonical pullback isomorphism. The existing pro-etale coefficient naturality theorem transports the whole morphism-family tensor presentation before applying naturality. This naturality and the derived coefficient tensor square identify the two transposes under the product-support adjunction. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves the supported exterior-product equality for unbounded inputs. Naturality of the support comparison at eF.inv and cancellation of eF.inv followed by eF.hom give the exact displayed bounded-presentation formula.

proof.text: Construct open pullback of pro-etale supported constants from closed base change and the canonical constant pullback, preserving quotient generators. Epimorphic quotient maps give uniqueness. Cancel the quotient in the comparison/open coefficient square, using the normalized etale open mate and the constant comparison square. The ordinary square of right mates derives to the support-restriction square, with the exact derived-composition and coefficient-pullback isomorphisms appearing in the statement.
